## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`list_orders` should take an offset, because the listing the title calls paginated can only return its first page. Issue #12 was not available, so that requirement is read from the pull-request title alone.

## Changes
The pull request adds `paginate(items, limit, offset=0)` in `app/paging.py` and gives `list_orders` an optional `limit` that it passes to that helper after sorting. It adds one limit test for `list_orders` and three tests for `paginate`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/orders.py:9 — correctness — Pass an offset through list_orders — A caller that needs orders 3 and 4 of 5 cannot get them: `list_orders(orders, limit=2)` always returns the newest two. Line 9 calls `paginate(ordered, limit)` with no offset, and `list_orders` has no parameter for one. — Clients of the order listing can cap results but cannot fetch any page after the first, so the pagination the title names is unreachable. — Fix: Add `offset=0` to `list_orders`, pass it to `paginate`, and extend `test_limit_caps_results` in `tests/test_orders.py` with a second-page case.

## Suggestions
- app/paging.py:12 — tests — Cover limit=0 in the paginate tests — `paginate([1, 2, 3], limit=0)` must return `[]`, but no test passes `limit=0` to `paginate` or `list_orders`; the tests use limits of 2, `None` and -1. Line 12 separates `0` from `None` only through `is None`. — A later change to a truthiness check would return every order for `limit=0` and no test would fail.

## Not reviewed
- The text of issue #12, which the pull-request body says this change closes, was not available in the checkout or in `../pr.json`.
